items.question: What inquiry does Goddess Gaurī make to Śaṅkara after bowing?
premises: Goddess Gaurī bows with her head
Gaurī addresses Śaṅkara directly
Gaurī initiates a question
items.inference: Gaurī respectfully approaches Śaṅkara to seek instruction.
items.plain_english: Having bowed with her head, the goddess Gaurī asks Śaṅkara.

rows.grounds: describes what is to be told; compound dharma+artha+sādhaka

items.question: What kind of teaching does Gaurī request from the lord of gods?
premises: Gaurī asks for favor
Gaurī addresses Śaṅkara as lord of gods
Gaurī requests instruction accomplishing duty and wealth
items.inference: Gaurī seeks a gracious teaching that accomplishes dharma and artha.
items.plain_english: Grant your favor, lord of gods, and tell me that which accomplishes dharma and wealth.

items.question: Which kinds of ritual practices does Gaurī ask Śaṅkara to explain?
premises: Pacifying rites are mentioned
Nourishing rites are mentioned
Many rites are requested
items.inference: Gaurī requests instruction on various rites including pacifying and nourishing ones.
items.plain_english: Tell me of pacifying and nourishing rites, and many other practices.

items.question: What impairments and obstructions does Gaurī want Śaṅkara to address?
premises: Loss of knowledge is named
Loss of action is named
Obstruction and other matters are included
items.inference: Gaurī seeks knowledge about losses, obstructions, and related issues.
items.plain_english: Tell me of the loss of knowledge, the loss of action, obstruction, and likewise other matters.

rows.grounds: refers to all requested topics; compound tat+sarva

items.question: What comprehensive instruction does Gaurī especially request from the lord?
premises: Mantra meditation is specifically requested
All previously mentioned topics are included
Gaurī directly asks the lord to speak
items.inference: Gaurī asks the lord to explain mantra meditation and all the requested matters.
items.plain_english: Especially tell me, lord, about mantra meditation and all of that.

items.question: What effect does mere knowledge of this teaching have on a human being?
premises: The teaching is referred to by a relative pronoun
Mere knowledge of it is sufficient
A human becomes rare on earth through it
items.inference: By merely knowing this teaching, a human becomes rare on earth.
items.plain_english: By the mere knowledge of which a human becomes rare on earth.

rows.grounds: content to be declared; compound tat+sarva

items.question: How does Śaṅkara respond to Gaurī’s request for comprehensive instruction?
premises: Śaṅkara promises to tell Gaurī
The content is all that was asked
The teaching is presented as declared
items.inference: Śaṅkara agrees to declare all the requested teachings to Gaurī.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, goddess, all that has been declared.

items.question: From what source and for what reason does Śaṅkara present this teaching?
premises: The essence is drawn from Uḍḍīśa
Śaṅkara speaks the teaching
The teaching is given because of Gaurī’s devotion
items.inference: Śaṅkara conveys the essence drawn from Uḍḍīśa out of devotion to Gaurī.
items.plain_english: Having drawn the essence from Uḍḍīśa, I have spoken it to you out of devotion.

items.question: Which divine forms are invoked as removers of fear for all beings?
premises: Kapardin is named
Virūpākṣa is named
The invoked form removes fear of all beings
items.inference: Kapardin and Virūpākṣa are invoked as powers that remove fear from all beings.
items.plain_english: Kapardin, Virūpākṣa, the remover of fear from all beings.

items.question: What lethal effect is claimed when these powers are properly employed?
premises: The powers are employed as agents
They immediately destroy life-breaths
The result is stated without doubt
items.inference: When employed, these powers immediately kill, without doubt.
items.plain_english: When these are employed, they immediately destroy the life-breaths; there is no doubt.

items.question: Which third and fourth ritual operations are enumerated in this sequence?
premises: A third operation is named
A fourth operation is named
The operations are causing hatred and eradication
items.inference: The third operation is causing hatred and the fourth is eradication.
items.plain_english: The third is causing hatred, and likewise the fourth is eradication.

items.question: What additional powers over fire and beings are listed in this teaching?
premises: Paralyzing of fire is mentioned
Supreme subjugation is mentioned
Both are presented as further operations
items.inference: The teaching includes paralyzing fire and supreme subjugation.
items.plain_english: And then that which paralyzes fire, and supreme subjugation.

items.question: Where and by whom were these yogic practices authoritatively declared?
premises: Śiva is the speaker
The practices are called yogas
They are declared in Uḍḍīśa as scriptural determination
items.inference: Śiva declared these yogas in the authoritative teaching of Uḍḍīśa.
uncertainties: uḍḍīśe may refer to a place or a textual tradition
items.plain_english: These practices were told by Śiva in Uḍḍīśa, in the determined scripture.

items.question: What harmful effects on spirits and weapons are attributed to these practices?
premises: Causing spirit-fever is named
Spoiling missiles and weapons is named
Both are presented as operations
items.inference: The practices can cause spirit-fever and spoil missiles and weapons.
items.plain_english: The causing of spirit-fever and the spoiling of missiles and weapons.

items.question: What destructive and agitating effects on beings are included among these operations?
premises: Destruction is named
Causing madness is named
Enraging elephants and horses is named
items.inference: The operations include destruction, maddening, and enraging elephants and horses.
items.plain_english: Destruction, causing madness, and enraging elephants and horses.

items.question: What destructive acts involving fire and leaves may a practitioner perform?
premises: Destruction of fire is stated
An optative injunction is given
Destruction of leaves is also stated
items.inference: One may perform the destruction of fire and indeed the destruction of leaves.
items.plain_english: One should bring about the destruction of fire and indeed the destruction of leaves.

items.question: What supernatural attainments and fiery phenomena are attributed to this knowledge?
premises: Attainment of vetāla sandals is named
Blazing from a meteor is named
Both are included as results
items.inference: The knowledge yields vetāla-sandal attainment and blazing like a meteor.
uncertainties: ulvakājjvalanaṃ may indicate blazing from or like a meteor
items.plain_english: The attainment of vetāla sandals and likewise blazing from a meteor.

items.question: What kinds of applications and substances are included in these magical operations?
premises: Applications of vidyā and mantra are named
Herbs are included
These are characterized as magical
items.inference: The operations include vidyā-mantra applications and magical herbs.
uncertainties: ābhicārikān may qualify herbs, applications, or both
items.plain_english: Applications of vidyā and mantra and other such things, and magical herbs.

items.question: What limitation is asserted for someone who lacks knowledge of Uḍḍīśa?
premises: A person may not know Uḍḍīśa
Such a person may be angry
Anger without this knowledge is ineffective
items.inference: One who does not know Uḍḍīśa can accomplish nothing even in anger.
items.plain_english: He who does not know Uḍḍīśa—what can he do, even if angry?

items.question: What extraordinary power is claimed as a true result of this knowledge?
premises: Causing the sun to fall to earth is stated
The claim is explicitly affirmed
The statement denies falsehood
items.inference: The teaching claims the power to bring down the sun, and asserts this is not false.
items.plain_english: One could even cause the sun to fall to the earth; this will not be false.

items.question: To which divine weapons are these practices compared for their force?
premises: Yama’s staff is invoked as comparison
Kubera’s mace is invoked as comparison
Comparisons imply great power
items.inference: The practices are likened in force to the staff of Yama and the mace of Kubera.
items.plain_english: As is the staff of Yama, and as is the mace of Kubera.

items.question: Which additional divine weapon-bearer completes the comparison of power?
premises: The trident-holder is named
The verse continues the comparison series
The reference implies formidable power
items.inference: The comparison extends to the weapon of the trident-holder.
uncertainties: The compared weapon is implied rather than explicitly named
items.plain_english: As is that of the trident-holder.

items.question: How effective are these great practices when directed against an enemy?
premises: The practices are called great yogas
They are compared to divine weapons
They are employed for the sake of an enemy
items.inference: When employed against an enemy, these great practices are as powerful as divine weapons.
items.plain_english: Likewise, these great practices, when employed against an enemy, are of such power.

items.question: Under what conditions do these employed practices achieve success?
premises: The practitioner is satisfied
The practices are properly employed
They are applied with good consideration
items.inference: These practices succeed when employed by a satisfied practitioner with careful consideration.
items.plain_english: When employed by one who is satisfied and acts with good consideration, they succeed.
